115	        progress.orientation = .horizontal
116	        progress.spacing = 4
117	        // A row in the leading-aligned card hugs its content, or its width is
118	        // ambiguous (an NSStackView's hugging is `setHuggingPriority`).
119	        progress.setHuggingPriority(.defaultHigh, for: .horizontal)
120	
121	        buttonRow.orientation = .horizontal
122	        buttonRow.spacing = 6
123	        buttonRow.setHuggingPriority(.defaultHigh, for: .horizontal)
124	        for kind in TutorialPanelButton.allCases {
125	            let style: StickerButton.Style =
126	                kind == .showMe || kind == .next || kind == .openPractice ? .primary : .secondary
127	            let button = StickerButton(
128	                title: kind.title, style: style, target: self, action: #selector(pressed(_:)))
129	            button.setAccessibilityIdentifier("tutorial." + kind.rawValue)
130	            buttons[kind] = button
131	        }
132	
133	        card.orientation = .vertical
134	        card.alignment = .leading
135	        card.spacing = 8
136	        card.edgeInsets = NSEdgeInsets(
137	            top: Self.inset, left: Self.inset, bottom: Self.inset, right: Self.inset)
138	        for view in [titleLabel, progress, textLabel, messageLabel, buttonRow] as [NSView] {
139	            card.addArrangedSubview(view)
140	        }
141	        for view in [titleLabel, textLabel, messageLabel] as [NSView] {
142	            view.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: width).isActive = true
143	        }
144	        card.setCustomSpacing(14, after: messageLabel)
145	        card.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
146	        card.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.cardWidth).isActive = true
147	
148	        // The card pinned at the top-left of a plain root, the window sized to
149	        // its fitting size (the recorder panel's rule).
150	        let root = NSView()
151	        root.addSubview(card)
152	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
153	            card.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: root.topAnchor),
154	            card.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: root.leadingAnchor),
155	        ])
156	        panel.contentView = root
157	    }
158	
159	    @objc private func pressed(_ sender: NSButton) {
160	        guard let kind = buttons.first(where: { $0.value === sender })?.key else { return }
161	        onPress?(kind)
162	    }
163	
164	    // MARK: - Showing
165	
166	    /// The runner's state, or — when it just left a step by its met wait —
167	    /// that step with the tick for `tickHold` first. Only a completed list
168	    /// that GREW ticks: Back shortens it to an earlier step, which is no
169	    /// step just left.
170	    func showStep(_ runner: TutorialRunner) {
171	        self.runner = runner
172	        let id = ObjectIdentifier(runner)
173	        let last = runner.lastCompleted
174	        let before = seen
175	        seen = last.map { (id, $0.step, $0.by) }
176	        if let last, last.by == .wait,
177	           before == nil || before?.runner != id || last.step > (before?.step ?? 0)
178	        {
179	            showTick(runner, step: last.step)
180	            return
181	        }
182	        if before?.runner != id { cancelTick() }
183	        if ticking { return }
184	        render(runner)
185	    }
186	
187	    /// An offer: what is missing and the practice project (spec §11 TU-5,
188	    /// TU-10 (2)).
189	    func showOffer(title: String, sentence: String, message: String?, tutorial: String? = nil) {
190	        cancelTick()
191	        tickView.isHidden = true
192	        runner = nil
193	        seen = nil
194	        mode = "offer"
195	        tutorialID = tutorial
196	        titleLabel.stringValue = title
197	        progressLabel.stringValue = ""
198	        progressLabel.isHidden = true
199	        setText(sentence)
200	        setMessage(message)
201	        setButtons([.openPractice, .close], enabled: [.openPractice, .close])
202	        fit()
203	    }
204	
205	    private func render(_ runner: TutorialRunner) {
206	        let tutorial = runner.tutorial
207	        tutorialID = tutorial.id
208	        titleLabel.stringValue = TutorialCoach.displayTitle(tutorial.title)
209	        progressLabel.isHidden = false
210	        tickView.isHidden = true
211	        buttons[.exit]?.title = runner.finished ? "Done" : TutorialPanelButton.exit.title
212	        if runner.finished {
213	            mode = "finished"
214	            progressLabel.stringValue = "Finished"
215	            setText("You finished this tutorial.")
216	            setMessage(Self.message(runner))
217	            setButtons([.back, .exit], enabled: [.back, .exit])
218	        } else {
219	            mode = "step"
220	            progressLabel.stringValue = "Step \(runner.index + 1) of \(tutorial.steps.count)"
221	            setText(runner.currentStep.text)
222	            setMessage(Self.message(runner))
223	            let offered = runner.offers.compactMap(TutorialPanelButton.init(rawValue:))
224	            setButtons(offered, enabled: runner.showMeRunning ? [.exit] : Set(offered))
225	        }
226	        fit()
227	    }
228	
229	    private func showTick(_ runner: TutorialRunner, step: Int) {
230	        let tutorial = runner.tutorial
231	        guard step >= 1, step <= tutorial.steps.count else {
232	            render(runner)
233	            return
234	        }
235	        cancelTick()
236	        ticking = true
237	        mode = "step"
238	        tutorialID = tutorial.id
239	        titleLabel.stringValue = TutorialCoach.displayTitle(tutorial.title)
240	        progressLabel.isHidden = false
241	        progressLabel.stringValue = "Step \(step) of \(tutorial.steps.count)"
242	        tickView.isHidden = false
243	        setText(tutorial.steps[step - 1].text)
244	        setButtons(shown, enabled: [])
245	        fit()
246	        tickTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: Self.tickHold, repeats: false) {
247	            [weak self] _ in
248	            guard let self else { return }
249	            self.ticking = false
250	            self.tickTimer = nil
251	            if let runner = self.runner { self.render(runner) }
252	        }
253	    }
254	
255	    private func cancelTick() {
256	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
257	        tickTimer = nil
258	        ticking = false
259	    }
260	
261	    /// The first that holds: the last Show Me's error on its own step, where
262	    /// a Show Me export was sent, the reveal's refusal.
263	    private static func message(_ runner: TutorialRunner) -> String? {
264	        if let last = runner.lastShowMe, let error = last.error, !runner.finished,
265	           last.step == runner.index + 1
266	        {
267	            return error
268	        }
269	        if let path = runner.lastShowMe?.paths.last {
270	            return "Show Me exports to \((path as NSString).abbreviatingWithTildeInPath)."
271	        }
272	        return runner.revealRefused
273	    }
274	
275	    private func setText(_ text: String) {
276	        plainText = TutorialSentence.plain(text)
277	        textLabel.attributedStringValue = TutorialSentence.attributed(
278	            text, font: DS.sans(13), boldFont: DS.sans(13, weight: .semibold),
279	            codeFont: DS.mono(12), color: DS.textStrong)
280	    }
281	
282	    private func setMessage(_ text: String?) {
283	        message = text
284	        messageLabel.stringValue = text ?? ""
285	        messageLabel.isHidden = text == nil
286	    }
287	
288	    private func setButtons(_ list: [TutorialPanelButton], enabled: Set<TutorialPanelButton>) {
289	        shown = list
290	        for view in buttonRow.arrangedSubviews { buttonRow.removeArrangedSubview(view) }
291	        for view in buttonRow.subviews { view.removeFromSuperview() }
292	        for kind in list {
293	            guard let button = buttons[kind] else { continue }
294	            button.isEnabled = enabled.contains(kind)
295	            buttonRow.addArrangedSubview(button)
296	        }
297	    }
298	
299	    /// Sized to the card, keeping the top-left (the recorder panel's rule).
300	    private func fit() {
301	        guard let window else { return }
302	        card.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
303	        let size = card.fittingSize
304	        var frame = window.frameRect(forContentRect: NSRect(origin: .zero, size: size))
305	        let current = window.frame
306	        frame.origin = NSPoint(x: current.minX, y: current.maxY - frame.height)
307	        window.setFrame(frame, display: window.isVisible)
308	    }
309	
310	    // MARK: - The dev tools' reads
311	
312	    /// `tutorial_state`'s and `tutorial_press`'s `panel`.
313	    func state() -> [String: Any] {
314	        [
315	            "shown": window?.isVisible ?? false,
316	            "mode": mode,
317	            "tutorial": tutorialID.map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
318	            "title": titleLabel.stringValue,
319	            "progress": progressLabel.isHidden ? "" : progressLabel.stringValue,
320	            "text": plainText,
321	            "message": message.map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
322	            "buttons": shown.map(\.rawValue),
323	            "enabled": shown.filter { buttons[$0]?.isEnabled == true }.map(\.rawValue),
324	            "tick": ticking,
325	            "project": projectPath?().map { $0 as Any } ?? NSNull(),
326	        ]
327	    }
328	
329	    /// The button, when it is shown and enabled.
330	    func button(_ b: TutorialPanelButton) -> NSButton? {
331	        guard shown.contains(b), let button = buttons[b], button.isEnabled else { return nil }
332	        return button
333	    }
334	}

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

  presets and is not edited by a look.

  `normalized` (lowercased, punctuation and whitespace trimmed both ends),
  `isFiller`, and `MediaTranscript.captionWords(for:in:)`, `words(for:in:)`
  with the fillers removed — every caption producer reads it, so a
  disfluent transcript captions as before.

  (spec §11 TR-5, TR-11): a clip's words in TIMELINE times, each marked
  `filler`, for the assistant's false starts. The cache door reads the cloud
  transcript when its marker serves `.captions` (`cloudWords`); otherwise the
  on-device engine runs over the clip's window off the main thread
  (`deviceWords`, `recognize`), never downloading a model; never the
  network. The handler's first line reads

  the assistant's Stop ends the run (amends AI-16). An optional `from`/`to`

  window plus `recognitionPadSeconds` each side (`recognitionJob`).

  on-device recogniser heard (spec §11 TR-14): one file per media and
  language in the package's `cache/device-transcripts/`, keyed by the
  file's source stamp, the language, the OS version and `version`, each run
  a heard source span and its words in source ticks. `heard(...)` answers
  from a stored run that contains the call's span, else recognises and
  stores (dropping runs the new one contains), never after a cancel or a
  file change during the run; written through `CacheLedger`. Captions,
  the filler tools and the cloud readers never read it.

  synchronous so it runs on whichever engine thread calls it:
  `normalize` (trim, split, sort, the per-engine `lead` — its ONE home —
  and the clamp into the job's `span`, a word pushed off the end on the
  clip's last frame), the pager (speaker, 0.25 s gap, sentence mark,
  3 s, `maxWords`, and the MEASURED width through
  `LayerRenderers.measuredSize`), the balance step once per width
  break, the clause preference, shrink-then-wrap for a lone word, and
  page timing that abuts under `breakGap` and never passes the span.
  `cues(...)` is what both engines call: `.subtitles` goes to
  `CaptionCues.build`, untouched. `samplePage` is `cues(...)`'s first page

  balance step included. Pauses are word gaps and punctuation;
  `SilenceDetector`/`MediaSpeech` are not consulted.

for name in names + sections + ["clip:$selection"]:
            got = self.state(target=name)["target"]
            expect(got["name"] == name, f"asked {name}, answered {got['name']}")
            if name.startswith("inspector.tab."):
                index = ["clip", "media", "document", "assistant"].index(name.split(".")[-1])
                x, y, w, h = tabs[0]["frame"]
                width = w / 4
                left, right = swift_round(index * width), swift_round((index + 1) * width)
                want = dump.clipped(tabs[0], [x + left, y, right - left, h])
                expect(near(got["rect"], want), f"{name}: {got['rect']}, the strip's {want}")
            elif name.startswith("inspector.sub_tab."):
                sub = name.split(".")[-1]
                if sub not in offered:
                    expect(got["rect"] is None and got["reason"],
                           f"{name}: un-offered, answered {got['rect']} {got['reason']!r}")
                    continue
                x, y, w, h = subs[0]["frame"]
                step = (w - 2 * 10 - 1) / len(offered)
                i = offered.index(sub)
                left = 10 + swift_round(i * step)
                right = 10 + swift_round((i + 1) * step) + 1
                want = dump.clipped(subs[0], [x + left, y + 8, right - left, 24])
                expect(near(got["rect"], want), f"{name}: {got['rect']}, the strip's {want}")
            elif name == "clip:$selection":
                lanes = dump.expected("timeline.clips")
                r = got["rect"]
                expect(r is not None and r[2] > 0 and r[3] > 0, f"{name}: rect {r}")
                expect(intersect(r, lanes) is not None and near(intersect(r, lanes), r),
                       f"{name}: {r} not inside timeline.clips {lanes}")
            else:
                if name in names:
                    expect(dump.shown(name), f"{name}: no shown view carries it in the dump")
                want = self.compare_target(name, dump, got)
                if name.startswith("section:"):
                    frame = dump.shown(name)[0]["frame"] if dump.shown(name) else None
                    if want is None or not near(want, frame):
                        clipped.append(name)
        expect(clipped, "precondition: no Sound section is clipped or hidden")
        print(f"    K1 precondition: clipped or hidden {clipped}", flush=True)
        self.call("perform_menu_item", path=["File", "Export…"])
        sheet, _ = self.capture("sheet", "k1-sheet")
        sheet_names = [n for n in fixed_names() if n.startswith(SHEET_PREFIX)]
        for name in sheet_names:
            got = self.state(target=name)["target"]
            expect(sheet.shown(name), f"{name}: no shown view carries it in the sheet's dump")
            expect(got["window"] == "sheet" or got["rect"] is None,
                   f"{name}: window {got['window']}")
            self.compare_target(name, sheet, got)
        self.call("cancel_sheet")
        return (f"{len(names)} fixed names, {len(sections)} Sound sections, clip:$selection and "
                f"{len(sheet_names)} sheet controls match the dump; clipped {clipped}")

    # ---- M rows ----

    def m_row(self, tid):
        started = self.start(tid)
        opened = [w["kind"] for w in started.get("windows_opened", [])]
        expect("tutorial" in opened, f"the menu start opened {opened}")
        notes, presses = [], 0
        sheet_steps = set()
        export_id = None
        while presses < 12:
            got = self.settled()
            expect(got.get("running"), f"not running: {got}")
            panel = got["panel"]
            if got.get("finished"):
                break
            k, n = got["step"], got["steps"]
            expect(panel["mode"] == "step" and panel["progress"] == f"Step {k} of {n}",
                   f"step {k}: panel {panel['mode']} {panel['progress']!r}")
            expect(panel["text"] == plain(got["text"]),
                   f"step {k}: text {panel['text']!r}, want {plain(got['text'])!r}")
            expect(panel["buttons"] == got["offers"],
                   f"step {k}: buttons {panel['buttons']}, offers {got['offers']}")
            notes.append(self.ring_matches(got, tid, k))
            if (got.get("ring") or {}).get("window") == "sheet":
                sheet_steps.add(k)
            action = next(a for a in ("show_me", "next", "skip") if a in got["offers"])
            answer = self.press(action)
            presses += 1
            last = answer.get("last_show_me") or {}
            if action == "show_me":
                expect(last.get("ok") is True, f"step {k}'s Show Me failed: {last.get('error')}")
                if last.get("paths"):
                    try:
                        export_id = json.loads(last["results"][-1]).get("export_id")
                    except (ValueError, IndexError, AttributeError):
                        export_id = None
        got = self.settled()
        panel = got["panel"]
        expect(got.get("finished") and panel["mode"] == "finished"
               and panel["buttons"] == ["back", "exit"],
               f"the end: finished {got.get('finished')}, panel {panel['mode']} "
               f"{panel['buttons']}")
        if tid == "export.range":
            expect(sheet_steps == {4, 5}, f"the ring was in the sheet at steps {sheet_steps}")
            want = "Show Me exports to ~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4."
            expect(panel["message"] == want, f"finished message {panel['message']!r}")
            expect(export_id is not None, "no export id in the Show Me's results")
            self.client.wait_export(export_id, seconds=180)
            written = HOME / "Movies" / "Frame Job Tutorial.mp4"
            expect(written.exists() and written.stat().st_size > 0, f"{written} not written")
        return f"{presses} presses to the finish; " + "; ".join(notes)

    # ---- the other rows ----

    def at_step2(self):
        self.start("audio.volume")
        self.call("set_selection", clips=[self.ids[0]])
        got = self.settled(want_step=2)
        expect(got.get("step") == 2 and not got["panel"]["tick"],
               f"volume is at step {got.get('step')}, tick {got['panel']['tick']}")
        return got

    def tk1(self):
        self.start("audio.volume")
        first = self.settled(want_step=1)
        expect(first.get("step") == 1, f"started at step {first.get('step')}")
        self.call("set_selection", clips=[self.ids[0]])
        ticked = self.state()["panel"]
        expect(ticked["tick"] is True and ticked["progress"] == "Step 1 of 3",
               f"after the selection: tick {ticked['tick']}, {ticked['progress']!r}")
        expect(ticked["enabled"] == [], f"buttons enabled during the tick: {ticked['enabled']}")
        time.sleep(1.5)
        later = self.state()["panel"]
        expect(later["tick"] is False and later["progress"] == "Step 2 of 3",
               f"1.5 s later: tick {later['tick']}, {later['progress']!r}")
        # Back shortens the completed list to an earlier met wait: no tick.
        shown = self.press("show_me").get("last_show_me") or {}
        expect(shown.get("ok") is True, f"step 2's Show Me failed: {shown.get('error')}")
        third = self.settled(want_step=3)
        expect(third.get("step") == 3, f"after step 2's Show Me: step {third.get('step')}")
        self.press("back")
        back = self.state()
        panel = back["panel"]
        expect(back.get("step") == 2 and panel["tick"] is False
               and panel["progress"] == "Step 2 of 3",
               f"after Back from step 3: step {back.get('step')}, tick {panel['tick']}, "
               f"{panel['progress']!r}")
        return ("the tick held step 1 with every button off, then step 2; Back from step 3 "
                "showed step 2 with no tick")

    def w1(self):
        got = self.at_step2()
        dump, _ = self.capture("editor", "w1-before")

590	                f"{len(sheet_names)} sheet controls match the dump; clipped {clipped}")

593	
594	    def m_row(self, tid):
595	        started = self.start(tid)
596	        opened = [w["kind"] for w in started.get("windows_opened", [])]
597	        expect("tutorial" in opened, f"the menu start opened {opened}")
598	        notes, presses = [], 0
599	        sheet_steps = set()
600	        export_id = None
601	        while presses < 12:
602	            got = self.settled()
603	            expect(got.get("running"), f"not running: {got}")
604	            panel = got["panel"]
605	            if got.get("finished"):
606	                break
607	            k, n = got["step"], got["steps"]
608	            expect(panel["mode"] == "step" and panel["progress"] == f"Step {k} of {n}",
609	                   f"step {k}: panel {panel['mode']} {panel['progress']!r}")
610	            expect(panel["text"] == plain(got["text"]),
611	                   f"step {k}: text {panel['text']!r}, want {plain(got['text'])!r}")
612	            expect(panel["buttons"] == got["offers"],
613	                   f"step {k}: buttons {panel['buttons']}, offers {got['offers']}")
614	            notes.append(self.ring_matches(got, tid, k))
615	            if (got.get("ring") or {}).get("window") == "sheet":
616	                sheet_steps.add(k)
617	            action = next(a for a in ("show_me", "next", "skip") if a in got["offers"])
618	            answer = self.press(action)
619	            presses += 1
620	            last = answer.get("last_show_me") or {}
621	            if action == "show_me":
622	                expect(last.get("ok") is True, f"step {k}'s Show Me failed: {last.get('error')}")
623	                if last.get("paths"):
624	                    try:
625	                        export_id = json.loads(last["results"][-1]).get("export_id")
626	                    except (ValueError, IndexError, AttributeError):
627	                        export_id = None
628	        got = self.settled()
629	        panel = got["panel"]
630	        expect(got.get("finished") and panel["mode"] == "finished"
631	               and panel["buttons"] == ["back", "exit"],
632	               f"the end: finished {got.get('finished')}, panel {panel['mode']} "
633	               f"{panel['buttons']}")
634	        if tid == "export.range":
635	            expect(sheet_steps == {4, 5}, f"the ring was in the sheet at steps {sheet_steps}")
636	            want = "Show Me exports to ~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4."

638	            expect(export_id is not None, "no export id in the Show Me's results")
639	            self.client.wait_export(export_id, seconds=180)
640	            written = HOME / "Movies" / "Frame Job Tutorial.mp4"
641	            expect(written.exists() and written.stat().st_size > 0, f"{written} not written")
642	        return f"{presses} presses to the finish; " + "; ".join(notes)
